submission.bindingBasis: The owner action contract requires a compare-and-close against the exact expectedSourceStateDigest. The planning-time digest was sha256:e5d8008d... but the currentSourceStateDigest is sha256:79bcb09f... — a mismatch. A prior planning binding attempt already failed with REVISION_MISMATCH/not_committed. However, the consequence boundary evidence shows the tree bytes are identical (treeBefore == treeNow == 4ade3056...), and the only concurrent change was an empty Git commit that did not alter the tree content. The contract explicitly states that "after re-observation a caller may close against the new exact current digest." Therefore, re-observing to obtain the new exact current digest is the correct path to enable the intended close, rather than attempting another stale binding or rebasing unnecessarily.
submission.rationale: The planning-time digest no longer matches the current digest — a concurrent empty Git commit changed the head revision without changing tree content. The contract's compare-and-close is strict on the exact source state digest, and the prior binding attempt (REVISION_MISMATCH/not_committed) confirms the planning binding is stale. Per the contract, the proper corrective path is to re-observe the workspace to obtain the new exact current digest, then close against it. This preserves the intended consequence (close the workspace) without inventing APIs or making a false digest claim. REBASE_AND_ACT is not appropriate because there is no semantic content change to rebase onto — the tree bytes are identical.
